title: Driving Through Economic Fog (Still)
summary: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin delivered a speech on March 27, 2026, describing the current economic outlook as fog that has 'deepened and spread,' citing AI uncertainty and geopolitical tensions (Iran conflict driving oil prices) as key sources of uncertainty. Barkin noted the economy remains resilient with 2% GDP growth and a 4.4% unemployment rate, but characterized the labor market as fragile given near-zero employment growth and cautious hiring. Inflation remains nearly 1 percentage point above the 2% target. The speaker emphasized these are his personal views only, not official FOMC positions.
key_points: Barkin characterizes the economic outlook as fog that has 'deepened and spread' since his speech a year ago, citing AI and geopolitical uncertainty as primary drivers
GDP grew at 2% in 2025; consumers (70% of GDP) continue spending despite low sentiment due to good fundamentals: low unemployment, rising real wages, elevated asset values
Unemployment rate has held around 4.4% for six months, but employment growth is near zero; the low rate is sustained by reduced net migration and baby boomers aging out
Inflation remains nearly 1 percentage point above the Fed's 2% target, down from a peak over 7% in 2022
Oil prices have spiked due to Iran conflict; Barkin notes historical oil shocks are highly coincident with recessions (1974, 1979, 1990)
Businesses are cautious, sitting on the sidelines: not cutting back but not leaning into new investments or hiring
Barkin explicitly states these views are his alone and not those of the FOMC or Federal Reserve System
why_it_matters: Barkin's speech provides a detailed district-level read on the U.S. economy from a regional Fed president who participates in FOMC meetings. His characterization of the outlook as increasingly foggy, with AI uncertainty compounding geopolitical risks, suggests a more uncertain policy path ahead. The tension between resilient growth and a fragile labor market, combined with above-target inflation, complicates the rate decision calculus.
macro_context: Barkin describes a bifurcated economy: resilient consumer spending supported by solid fundamentals versus a fragile labor market with near-zero job growth. The Iran conflict has spiked oil prices, reintroducing supply-side inflation concerns alongside persistent services inflation. The speaker sees reasons for hope on inflation (shelter prices declining) but identifies the inflation path as the 'foggiest part' of the outlook.
